item.title: Charm and beauty production in pp collisions with ALICE
item.description: arXiv:2611.26017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Measurements of charm and beauty production in proton--proton (pp) collisions provide crucial tests of perturbative quantum chromodynamics (pQCD) and unique access to heavy-quark hadronisation. In this contribution, a selection of recent ALICE results, with emphasis on LHC Run 3 measurements, is presented. The transverse-momentum-differential production cross sections of prompt D mesons at $\sqrt{s}=5.36$ and 13.6 TeV and of fully reconstructed B mesons at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV are discussed together with comparisons to theoretical calculations. The rapidity dependence of charm and beauty production and the $\rm D^{*+}/D^0$ and $\rm \Lambda_c^+/D^0$ yield ratios provide complementary constraints on heavy-quark production and hadronisation. Measurements of the fractions of ${\rm J}/\psi$ and $\psi({\rm 2S})$ originating from beauty-hadron decays, and of the inclusive $\psi({\rm 2S})$-to-${\rm J}/\psi$ production ratio, further constrain the interplay between perturbative heavy-quark production and non-perturbative bound-state formation.

item.title: Observation of the electromagnetic Dalitz decay $J/\psi \rightarrow \mu^+ \mu^- \eta$
item.description: arXiv:2611.26209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using a data sample of $(8.998 \pm 0.039)\times10^9$ $J/\psi$ events collected by the BESIII detector at BEPCII, we report the observation of the electromagnetic Dalitz decay $J/\psi \to \mu^+ \mu^- \eta$ for the first time, with a statistical significance greater than 10$\sigma$. The branching fraction is measured to be $\mathcal{B}(J/\psi \to \mu^+ \mu^- \eta) = (3.05 \pm 0.14_{\rm stat.} \pm 0.13_{\rm syst.})\times 10^{-6}$. The ratio of this branching fraction to that of the corresponding radiative decay $J/\psi \to \gamma\eta$ is determined to be $\mathcal{B}(J/\psi \to \mu^+\mu^-\eta)/\mathcal{B}(J/\psi \to \gamma\eta) = (2.80 \pm 0.18) \times 10^{-3}$. Combining this result with the previous BESIII measurement of the $J/\psi \to e^+e^-\eta$ branching fraction yields $\mathcal{B}(J/\psi \to \mu^+\mu^-\eta)/\mathcal{B}(J/\psi \to e^+e^-\eta) = 0.219 \pm 0.020$. These results are consistent with the theoretical predictions based on the vector meson dominance model.

item.title: A Surrogate Detector Model for the MINERvA Open Dataset
item.description: arXiv:2611.26271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing availability of open neutrino data promises broader scrutiny of interaction models, but a critical barrier remains: mapping theoretical predictions into reconstructed observables, which previously required computationally intensive methods inaccessible outside the original experimental collaborations. In this work, we present a probabilistic surrogate of the MINERvA detector response, trained on an open simulation dataset to map generator-level final-state particles and interaction geometry to reconstructed observables, without relying on generator-specific interaction labels. We assess its fidelity through conditional response distributions, reconstructed observables, and classifier-based closure tests. We further demonstrate generalization beyond the limitations of conventional phase-space-dependent reweighting by withholding two-particle-two-hole interactions entirely from training and showing that the surrogate reproduces their reconstructed response within the estimated uncertainties. In an end-to-end application to MINERvA charged-current inclusive muon-neutrino data, we reproduce selection efficiencies and purities and forward-fold predictions from GENIE, NuWro, and GiBUU for direct comparison with measurements. By moving theoretical predictions into reconstructed space rather than unfolding the data, this work establishes a reusable interface between neutrino interaction models and experimental observations, expanding the scope of physics accessible through open datasets.

item.title: Progress in measurements of the CKM angle $\gamma$ and charm mixing at LHCb
item.description: arXiv:2611.26449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Measurements of the CKM angle $\gamma$ and of the charm mixing and $C\!P$-violation parameters enable stringent and complementary tests of the weak sector of the Standard Model. The two categories of measurements are intimately related, since they both depend on hadronic parameters of $D^0$ meson decays, and knowledge of charm mixing is required to determine $\gamma$. The progress made in these sectors at the LHCb experiment is reviewed, and a new simultaneous combination of all relevant LHCb measurements is presented. The combination includes measurements based on data collected during 2011-2018, as well as the first measurement of $\gamma$ with data collected in 2024. The results, $\gamma = (63.2^{+2.3}_{-2.2})^{\circ}$ modulo $180^{\circ}$, $x_{12} = (4.2^{+0.4}_{-0.5})\times10^{-3}$, $y_{12} = (6.18^{+0.17}_{-0.18})\times10^{-3}$, $\phi^M_2 = (4^{+11}_{-10})\,\mathrm{mrad}$ and $\phi^{\Gamma}_2 = (19^{+23}_{-24})\,\mathrm{mrad}$, are the most precise to date. The $CP$ asymmetries in $D^0\to K^+K^-$ and $D^0\to\pi^+\pi^-$ decays are also determined under different theoretical assumptions.

item.title: Another relation among the neutrino mass-squared differences?
item.description: arXiv:2601.18781v3 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Determining the absolute neutrino mass scale remains a compelling challenge in particle physics. Establishing precise mathematical connections among the neutrino masses could significantly facilitate this task and shed additional light on the underlying mass-generation mechanism. We highlight the possible existence of a simple algebraic relation between the mass-squared differences, $$\frac{\sqrt{\Delta m^2_{31}}+\sqrt{\Delta m^2_{21}}}{\sqrt{\Delta m^2_{31}}-\sqrt{\Delta m^2_{21}}}=\sqrt{2},$$ which agrees remarkably well with the best-fit values of recent global analyses of neutrino oscillation data. We then investigate the implications of adopting this relation and how it decreases the number of independent parameters in the neutrino sector. We demonstrate that there are alternative representations well known in quark and charged-lepton physics. Furthermore, we place a tight constraint on the solar neutrino mass splitting, $\Delta m^2_{21}=(7.445 \pm 0.062) \times 10^{-5} \text{ eV}^2$, and also obtain $\Delta m^2_{31}=(2.548 \pm 0.041) \times 10^{-3} \text{ eV}^2$. Next-generation reactor and accelerator neutrino experiments are expected to significantly reduce systematic uncertainties. In particular, the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) will measure these parameters independently of each other at the sub-percent level, thereby providing a stringent and direct test of our results.

item.title: Automate the geometric SMEFT at dimension eight
item.description: arXiv:2611.25016v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present the first complete dimension-eight implementation of the geometric Standard Model Effective Field Theory (geoSMEFT) as UFO models for event generators such as MadGraph. The models contain all 674 baryon-number-conserving operators, with minimal flavour violation for the fermionic operators, and are also provided in the Murphy basis. We include dimension-six contributions and electroweak input-parameter corrections consistently through order $1/\Lambda^4$, and provide dimension-eight squared contributions as a diagnostic of EFT truncation. We validate the implementation against independent calculations and Ward identities. To make these models practical for collider studies, we develop a standalone tool that identifies all operators contributing to a given process at tree level, including those entering through input-parameter shifts. It reports their expected energy scaling and generates a restriction card to reduce the computational cost of event generation. The same geometric construction allows us to calculate two- and three-point functions beyond dimension eight, to arbitrary order in $1/\Lambda^2$. The models and the tool are publicly available.

item.title: Resonance-aware NLOPS matching for off-shell $t\bar t+tW$ production in association with a Higgs boson
item.description: arXiv:2611.25044v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a new NLO QCD Monte Carlo generator for the complete off-shell final state encompassing $t\bar tH$ and $tWH$ production with dileptonic decays, matched to parton showers in the resonance-aware POWHEG-RES framework. At Born level the calculation corresponds to the process $pp\to b\bar b\,e^+\nu_e\,\mu^-\bar\nu_\mu\,H$ in the four-flavour scheme with massive $b$ quarks. The complete matrix elements include all double-resonant, single-resonant and non-resonant topologies, all interferences and spin correlations, with both top quarks and $W$ bosons treated in the complex-mass scheme. This approach provides a unified and consistent treatment of $t\bar{t} H$ and $tWH$ production modes without the need for a diagram-removal or diagram-subtraction prescription. The generator, dubbed $\texttt{bb4lH}$, is implemented in the POWHEG-RES framework with OpenLoops amplitudes, and takes advantage of the multiple-radiation scheme ($\texttt{allrad}$) and of matrix-element-based resonance projectors. Semileptonic events are also supported and can be obtained from dileptonic ones, including QCD radiation in the hadronic $W$-boson decay. In addition, we present two new on-shell POWHEG generators for $t\bar{t} H$ and $tWH$ production, the latter being the first of its kind. We validate all generators against known fixed-order results and in the narrow-width limit, and present NLO and NLOPS predictions for the LHC in the dileptonic and semileptonic channels. Tuned comparisons with the corresponding on-shell descriptions show good agreement for inclusive observables, while sizeable differences arise in observables sensitive to the reconstructed top-quark line shape and in $tWH$-enriched regions. These findings are of direct relevance for the LHC analysis of $t\bar{t} H$ events and for the separation of $t\bar{t} H$ and $tWH$ production.

item.title: The BSM Rollercoaster, 1980-2000
item.description: arXiv:2611.25060v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This contribution is a personal historical retrospective on beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) physics from 1978 to the early 2000s, organized around its emotional rollercoaster. I trace two waves of optimism separated by a multiyear contraction of confidence, both ultimately ending in disappointment when decisive experimental confirmation failed to arrive. The story begins in 1978, when the Standard Model emerged as the front-runner. It then moves from the first wave of excitement over naturalness and Technicolor, rumored proton-decay events, and the construction of the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model, to the contraction of confidence in the late 1980s. A dramatic revival came in 1991, when the LEP and SLC precision data pointed toward supersymmetric unification, but it eventually gave way to renewed disappointment over the absence of superpartners and the sharpening of the LEP paradox. I also describe how the realization that Newtonian gravity had been tested only down to distances of order centimeters opened the door to large extra dimensions. Finally, I discuss how Weinberg's 1987 anthropic argument for the cosmological constant, the 1998 discovery of cosmic acceleration, and the emergence of the string landscape changed the intellectual status of naturalness itself and led to Split Supersymmetry. I have tried to describe not only what was proposed, but why these ideas felt compelling at the time, why confidence rose and fell, and how later evidence changed our sense of what could count as an explanation.

item.title: Measurements of inclusive $J/\psi$ production in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$ = 14.6, 17.3, 19.6, and 27 GeV with the STAR experiment
item.description: arXiv:2611.25487v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Inclusive $J/\psi$ production at mid-rapidity ($|y| < 1.0$) in Au+Au collisions at center-of-mass energies per nucleon-nucleon pair ($\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$) of 14.6, 17.3, 19.6, and 27 GeV is measured with the STAR detector at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider. The nuclear modification factor $R_{{\rm AA}}$ is used to quantify modifications of $J/\psi$ production relative to an interpolated $p$+$p$ reference. The measured $R_{{\rm AA}}$ shows a hint of a decreasing trend from peripheral to central collisions, reaching a value of approximately 0.5 in the 0-20% centrality class across all collision energies. Unlike similar measurements in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}}$ = 200 GeV, where $J/\psi$ $R_{{\rm AA}}$ shows little dependence on transverse momentum ($p_{\rm {T}}$), the corresponding $R_{{\rm AA}}$ at the lower collision energies of 14.6-27 GeV shows a tendency to increase with $p_{\rm {T}}$. Additionally, the inclusive $J/\psi$ $R_{{\rm AA}}$, integrated over $J/\psi$ $p_{\rm {T}}$, in central collisions exhibits no significant variation within uncertainties over the energy range of 14.6 to 200 GeV. These results can be qualitatively described by transport models that incorporate hot and cold nuclear matter effects.

item.title: Particle physics science communication with grass-roots Instagram: a success story
item.description: arXiv:2611.25806v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Communicating science to the public is an integral part of the work of a research collaboration, not an afterthought. Institutional and collaboration-level social media accounts are often run by professional communicators rather than by practising scientists, and single-scientist ``influencer'' accounts are demanding to sustain. We describe {\em CMSatDESY}, a crowd-sourced Instagram account on which the CMS group at DESY tells its own stories, each member in their own voice. In the first half of 2026, the science communication activities through this reached 140k+ unique accounts and received 250k+ views, with an engagement rate of 7\%. We discuss experiences and best practices that can be used by other groups, and describe how the account doubles as a science communication playground for outreach training for a large particle physics group.
item.dc:creator: Freya Blekman, Lucia Coll Saravia

item.title: Resonant Cavity Searches for Millicharged Dark Matter
item.description: arXiv:2611.25846v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A plethora of resonant cavity experiments have been designed to search for ultralight dark matter (DM) candidates, such as axion or dark-photon DM. In this work, we show that these same apparatuses can be sensitive to ultralight millicharged dark matter (mDM) with masses $m_\phi\sim1-100\,\mu\mathrm{eV}$. Similar to axion DM, in the presence of a background magnetic field, mDM acts as an effective current which can excite the modes of a resonant cavity. Importantly, for a cylindrical cavity, axion DM dominantly couples to the transverse magnetic (TM) modes, whereas mDM dominantly couples to the transverse electric (TE) modes. We project the sensitivity to mDM that resonant cavity experiments can achieve if they are able to tune and readout their TE modes. We find that fractional millicharges as small as $\epsilon_m=e_m/e\sim10^{-19}$ can be probed. If mDM constitutes only a subfraction $f_\mDM \lesssim0.2\%$ of the total DM density, competing astrophysical bounds do not apply. In this case, resonant cavities can be the most sensitive probes of mDM in this mass range.
item.dc:creator: Miguel Gonz\'alez Albert, Ariel Arza, Saarik Kalia

item.title: Inclusive and diffractive D meson photoproduction in $pPb$ collisions at the LHC using Pythia8 framework
item.description: arXiv:2611.25933v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a systematic analysis of inclusive and diffractive $D$-meson photoproduction in $ep$ and ultraperipheral $pPb$ collisions within the Pythia8 framework. Predictions obtained with different proton and Pomeron PDFs are compared with H1 measurements of inclusive and diffractive $D^*$ photoproduction at HERA. We also present predictions for the rapidity and transverse-momentum distributions of inclusive and diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction at the LHC. Our analysis indicates that the diffractive contribution exceeds 15\% at low $p_T$ and forward rapidities, suggesting that diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction could be accessible in future LHC runs. In addition, measurements of inclusive and diffractive $D^0$ photoproduction in ultraperipheral $pPb$ collisions can help constrain the proton and Pomeron PDFs.

item.title: Predictions for Inclusive Production Cross Sections of the Higgs Boson at the LHC and HL-LHC
item.description: arXiv:2611.26281v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present updated recommendations of the LHC Higgs Working Group (LHCHWG) for the inclusive production cross sections of a Standard Model Higgs boson in proton--proton collisions at centre-of-mass energies between $7$ and $14$ TeV, including the Run-3 energy of $13.6$ TeV, and for Higgs-boson masses between $120$ and $130$ GeV. All the major production modes are covered. The central values remain consistent with those of Yellow Report 4 (YR4) [arXiv:1610.07922] within the uncertainties quoted there, while the theoretical uncertainties are reduced for most production modes. The improvements rest on specific calculations rather than on a uniform advance: the complete N$^3$LO result in the heavy-top limit together with exact NNLO top-quark mass effects for gluon fusion; the N$^3$LO structure-function calculation supplemented by non-factorisable corrections for vector-boson fusion; the completion of the NLO QCD corrections to the loop-induced $gg\to ZH$ channel for $VH$; NNLO QCD matched to NNLL soft-gluon resummation and combined with NLO electroweak corrections for $t\bar{t}H$, and updated predictions for $tH$; and the matched four- and five-flavour-scheme prediction, with its explicit resummation-scale uncertainty, for $b\bar{b}H$. Since no PDF4LHC recommendation exists beyond NNLO, the mismatch between an N$^3$LO matrix element and NNLO distributions has to be carried as an uncertainty, estimated process by process: it is well determined for vector-boson fusion, whereas for gluon fusion it is doubled relative to YR4. PDFs are now the leading source of uncertainty for the most precisely predicted modes, while residual perturbative uncertainties dominate for the remainder. These results supersede the inclusive cross sections of YR4 and the ad interim recommendations of Ref. [arXiv:2402.09955], and form part of Report 5 of the LHCHWG.

item.title: Who Moved My $Z$ Boson? Revealing Resonance Features Inside a Neural Network
item.description: arXiv:2611.26291v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Methods used in mechanistic interpretability have revealed human-aligned concepts inside language and image models. In this paper, we search for physics concepts inside a neural a generative collider physics model trained on real LHC data (ShellFlow). We discover features inside ShellFlow that represent resonances, such as the $Z$, $J/\psi$, and $\Upsilon$. The network was never told which muons come from a resonance, it was only trained to generate the kinematics of the final-state particles. We use these features to alter aspects of the $Z$ boson: we change its mass between $\sim80$ and $105$ GeV, and removing such a feature from the neural network produces a broader $Z$ peak. In both cases the rest of the invariant mass spectrum remains mostly unchanged. The feature was built from the gradients of the neural network, and its selectivity was built using pattern recognition methods. A generative particle physics model trained on unlabeled data can be modified internally to change a physical quantity.

item.title: Compact GridPix Tracking: Test Beam Performance and Detector Response Modelling
item.description: arXiv:2611.26308v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We characterise a Timepix-based GridPix detector with a 21 mm drift length using 2.6 GeV electrons at ELSA. Tracks entering through the window at several angles are reconstructed as compact $\mu$TPC tracklets, providing position and local direction from one layer. Measured angular widths are approximately 5--10 mrad. An empirical response model calibrated to these data augments Geant4 ionisation information with gas-transport and readout effects, reproducing ten of twelve angular widths within approximately 20% and all spatial-residual widths within approximately 12%. Application without re-tuning to an independent 5 mm-drift measurement shows larger angular discrepancies. Our response model therefore provides input to feasibility studies of future compact tracking detectors.

item.title: Future avenues for precision oscillation measurements with compact movable reactors
item.description: arXiv:2611.26418v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: No planned neutrino experiment is expected to surpass Daya Bay's precision on $\thone$. Doing so requires innovative strategies to reduce statistical and systematic uncertainties. In this study, we consider a futuristic program with a movable reactor antineutrino source placed within short distances ($L\lesssim 3\,\km$) from the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO) detector. Due to the large fiducial mass of JUNO, even a relatively small reactor can produce a statistically significant number of events over a few years to probe the $\lesssim 8.7\% \,\nuebar$ disappearance set by $\thone$. We consider two possibilities: a $\mathcal{O}(20\mwth)$ microreactor in alcoves of the access tunnel to the underground laboratory, and a $\mathcal{O}(400 \mwth)$ unit on the surface. In both cases the reactor is observed by a small flux monitor detector near the source, while JUNO measures the antineutrino flux at two baselines, suppressing correlated flux and detector systematics. Using the measured Daya Bay per-isotope spectra and its covariance, we model a high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) core for the microreactor and a low-enriched uranium (LEU) core for the surface unit, and discuss various potential sources of systematic uncertainties and their impact on the precision of $\thone$. The underground microreactor could improve on JUNO's reach by a factor of three to four, to $\relsth \simeq 4\%$ over a decade, while the surface reactor would reach the present global-fit precision, $\relsth=2.5\%$, in about three years, provided the emission rate is monitored across reactor relocations to the sub-percent level.

item.title: Mono-Higgs signature in a singlet fermionic dark matter model
item.description: arXiv:2506.20113v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate mono-Higgs production as a probe of singlet fermionic dark matter (SFDM) at the LHC. In this framework, a Standard Model (SM) gauge-singlet Dirac fermion serves as the dark matter candidate, interacting with the visible sector through a real scalar mediator that mixes with the SM Higgs boson. Focusing on light dark matter with $M_\psi \in [0.1,10]$ GeV, we analyze the viable parameter space under constraints from relic density, Higgs decay properties, invisible decay bounds, rare $B$-meson decays, and direct detection experiments. We compute the mono-Higgs production cross sections at $\sqrt{s}=13~\mathrm{TeV}$ and compare approximate detector-level yields with the ATLAS $b\bar b$ search, supplemented by an inclusive upper bound for the CMS four-lepton channel. For the two benchmarks, the signal is dominated by non-resonant Higgs-pair production followed by an invisible Higgs decay. The resulting signal rate depends on both the production cross sections and the physical invisible branching fractions. The inclusive rates of $3.33$ and $1.43$~fb at loop-induced leading order provide quantitative signal targets before the visible Higgs decay and analysis cuts. For representative benchmark points satisfying the constraints considered, these comparisons indicate limited sensitivity in the analyzed channels. Nevertheless, the mono-Higgs channel provides a complementary probe of Higgs-portal dark matter scenarios, particularly in the low-mass mediator regime.
item.dc:creator: Yeong Gyun Kim, Kang Young Lee, Soo-hyeon Nam

item.title: Resurrecting Kaluza-Klein Dark Matter with Low-Temperature Reheating
item.description: arXiv:2602.12154v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In Universal Extra Dimension (UED) scenarios, the lightest Kaluza-Klein (KK) particle is naturally stable due to a remnant discrete symmetry, KK parity, arising from extra-dimensional compactification. This stability requires no ad hoc symmetry and renders Kaluza-Klein dark matter a well-motivated candidate, provided it reproduces the observed relic abundance. The minimal UED (mUED) framework being highly predictive is strongly constrained by the combined requirements of relic density and collider searches under standard cosmological assumptions. We revisit the dark matter phenomenology of mUED in the presence of a nonstandard cosmological history featuring a low reheating temperature driven by prolonged inflaton decay. Solving the coupled Boltzmann equations for dark matter, radiation, and inflaton energy densities, we show that entropy injection during reheating can dilute the relic abundance by orders of magnitude, reopening large regions of parameter space previously ruled out. We further demonstrate that the revived parameter space is consistent with current collider, direct-detection, and indirect-detection constraints, while remaining testable by upcoming experiments.
item.dc:creator: Kirtiman Ghosh, Abhishek Roy, Rameswar Sahu

item.title: $b\to c \bar u q$ decay and $CP$ violating observables in the presence of new physics contributions
item.description: arXiv:2605.22088v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, a comprehensive analysis for processes related to $b\to c\bar{u}q~(q=d, s)$ transitions is carried out, including new physics contributions. In light of a recent tension between branching fractions for $B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}^{(*)}M$ ($M=\pi, K$) decays in the QCD factorization approach and relevant experimental results, phenomenological constraints on complex-valued Wilson coefficients are discussed. Analyzed observables contain direct $CP$ asymmetry ($A_{\text{CP}}$) in $B^-\to D^0\pi^-$ decays and $\gamma/\phi_3$, one of the angles in the unitarity triangle, combined with others from $\tau_{B^+}/\tau_{B_d}$, $\Delta\Gamma_{q}/\Gamma_q$, and $A_{\rm SL}^{q}~(q=d, s)$. We constrain the complex Wilson coefficients at $1\sigma$ and $2\sigma$ levels under color-singlet and color-rearranged scenarios. These constraints yield correlated predictions for $\Delta\Gamma_d/\Gamma_d$, $A_{\rm SL}^d$ and $A_{\text{CP}}$.

item.title: Probing the dynamical inverse seesaw mechanism with low-frequency gravitational waves
item.description: arXiv:2605.27519v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the possibility of probing the dynamical inverse seesaw mechanism for the origin of light neutrino masses via the detection of stochastic gravitational waves (GW) in the low-frequency regime currently being probed by pulsar timing arrays. As the lepton number-violating term in inverse seesaw typically remains in the sub-MeV ballpark, its dynamical origin naturally brings the possibility of a low-scale first-order phase transition, which can be probed at low-frequency GW experiments. We also find interesting complementarity with heavy neutral lepton searches, as GW experiments remain sensitive to parameter space with small active-sterile mixing, which is out of reach for most particle physics experiments.

item.title: Qudit extension of parameterized IQP circuits: A generative quantum machine learning approach to integer data
item.description: arXiv:2606.28236v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Parameterized Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial (IQP) circuits have proven useful in quantum generative learning models, particularly for binary distributions. However, when applied to non-binary datasets, they exhibit notable limitations: mapping integer values into qubit-compatible binary representations often destroys the original metric structure of the data. In this paper we aim to extend them to a qudits formulation operating on an integer mapping of the data. The IQP quantum circuit is adapted to encode each integer valued pixel into a bit-string of fixed length and quantum gates are transformed to follow the qudit formalism. As a generative machine learning approach, a suitable loss function for the circuit training and the calculation of the covariance matrix among features are developed and validated on the energy deposits from single-particle electron showers in the electromagnetic calorimeter of the CLIC detector. The method proposed in this work can be also extended to other applications that utilize quantum generative machine learning for non-binary data.

item.title: A Paired Monte Carlo Intensity-Ratio Method for Incorporating Detector Resolution in Amplitude Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.20508v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Finite detector resolution can bias resonance parameters and fit fractions extracted from amplitude analyses. We present the paired Monte Carlo intensity-ratio method for incorporating resolution effects into amplitude analysis. The method uses ratios of reference intensities evaluated at paired truth-level and reconstructed kinematics to reweight the Monte Carlo normalization and approximately account for detector resolution. A resampling study of simulated $D^+\to K^+\pi^+\pi^-\pi^0$ decays shows that the method substantially reduces resolution-induced shifts in fitted resonance widths. Likelihood evaluation uses intensity calculations and normalization sums, avoiding a response convolution at each data event.
